description: Just the best at my work.
summary: The Space Repair Shop is a short animated story for school-age space fans. A computer repair technician receives five strange "repair tickets" one night, each for a machine NASA left behind: the Apollo 11 laser mirror and the Apollo lunar rovers on the Moon, the Opportunity rover and Ingenuity helicopter on Mars, and Voyager 1 in interstellar space. For each ticket, a hand-drawn chalk sketch and a retro "diagnostic screen" explain what the machine did and what science it made possible, backed by a real NASA photo and, for Mars, real sound recorded on Mars. The verdict is always the same: no repair needed, it already did its job. The story turns "space junk" into heroes that children can remember, and every fact in it is checked against NASA sources.
details:
WHAT IT IS

A 1 minute 52 second narrated, animated video in a hand-made paper and cardboard style, made for children aged about 8 to 13. It uses short sentences, one idea per screen, and a repeating pattern that is easy to follow.

WHY THIS IDEA

I repair laptops and computers for a living. Machines that stop working are my daily job, so I built the story around a repair shop to show children that some machines are not broken at all. They are finished.

HOW IT WORKS

Each of the five machines gets the same four beats:

1. A repair ticket types in: the item, where it is, when it was "dropped off", and the "problem".

2. A status stamp: Still Working, Silent, Retired, or Still Traveling.

3. A chalk drawing draws itself next to a diagnostic screen that answers two questions: "What it did" and "What we learned".

4. A real NASA photo and a verdict, with one fun fact.

THE FIVE MACHINES AND THE SCIENCE

- Apollo 11 laser mirror (Moon, 1969). Scientists still bounce lasers off it. It showed the Moon drifts away from Earth about 3.8 cm a year.

- Apollo lunar rovers (Moon, 1971 to 1972). They let astronauts travel far from the lander. On Apollo 17 the rover drove 35.9 km.

- Opportunity (Mars, 2004 to 2018). Built for 90 days, it explored for almost 15 years, drove 45.16 km, and its rocks showed water once sat on the surface of Mars.

- Ingenuity (Mars, 2021 to 2024). The first aircraft to make a powered, controlled flight on another planet. Planned for up to 5 flights, it flew 72.

- Voyager 1 (launched 1977). It flew past Jupiter and Saturn, entered interstellar space in 2012, and reaches one light-day from Earth on November 18, 2026.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

It is free to watch, needs no reading above primary-school level, and works with the sound off because every line is on screen. Each machine is a separate "ticket", so teachers can show one at a time. The Mars tickets let children hear real sound recorded on Mars.

HOW I MADE IT

I am a solo participant. I chose the challenge, based the story on my own work as a repair technician, asked for a hand-made look instead of smooth computer animation, and directed and reviewed every version. I used an AI assistant (Claude) as a tool to help develop the idea, write the Python code that draws the frames, and check facts against NASA pages. The video carries a small visible label saying so. The narration is an AI-generated voice (Kokoro text-to-speech), which is stated in the end credits and the file metadata. All photos are real NASA photos, and the music and every other sound are real recordings, not generated.

TOOLS

Python (Pillow and NumPy) to draw every frame, FFmpeg to encode the video and mix the sound, Kokoro text-to-speech for the narration.

NEXT STEPS

Add more tickets (Surveyor, Viking, Sojourner, Pioneer 10 and 11), record the narration in my own voice, and translate it into Sinhala and Tamil.
